explanation_en: This idiomatic expression is the direct equivalent of 'to bring to the table' or 'to put on the table.' It is used in political, social, and professional contexts to describe introducing a topic, debate, or proposal for consideration and discussion. It is highly common in news and editorial Spanish.

examples.en_text: The new director is bringing the issue of flexible hours back to the table.
examples.target_text: El nuevo director pone nuevamente sobre la mesa el tema de los horarios flexibles.

examples.en_text: The neighbors are bringing the problem of the lack of security in the neighborhood back to the table.
examples.target_text: Los vecinos ponen nuevamente sobre la mesa el problema de la falta de seguridad en el barrio.

examples.en_text: The latest newspaper article brought the debate on climate change back to the table.
examples.target_text: El último artículo del periódico puso nuevamente sobre la mesa el debate sobre el cambio climático.

examples.en_text: The teachers' strike has brought the need to improve schools back to the table.
examples.target_text: La huelga de profesores ha puesto nuevamente sobre la mesa la necesidad de mejorar las escuelas.

examples.en_text: If we want to travel this year, we have to bring the family budget back to the table.
examples.target_text: Si queremos viajar este año, tenemos que poner nuevamente sobre la mesa el presupuesto familiar.

examples.en_text: Yesterday's system crash brings the importance of having backups back to the table.
examples.target_text: La caída del sistema de ayer pone nuevamente sobre la mesa la importancia de tener copias de seguridad.

explanation_en: This compound preposition means 'in the midst of' or 'amid.' It can be used physically to mean 'in the middle of,' but is very frequently used in abstract contexts to describe a situation occurring during or surrounded by a specific emotional or social climate (e.g., 'en medio de la crisis'). It is a key connector for advanced narrative style.

examples.en_text: They found a small cabin in the middle of the forest.
examples.target_text: Encontraron una cabaña pequeña en medio del bosque.

examples.en_text: It is not easy to stay calm in the midst of a family argument.
examples.target_text: No es fácil mantener la calma en medio de una discusión familiar.

examples.en_text: The phone rang in the middle of the movie and annoyed everyone.
examples.target_text: El teléfono sonó en medio de la película y molestó a todos.

examples.en_text: She resigned from her job in the middle of the most important project of the year.
examples.target_text: Ella renunció a su trabajo en medio del proyecto más importante del año.

examples.en_text: The car broke down in the middle of the highway and we had to call the tow truck.
examples.target_text: El coche se averió en medio de la carretera y tuvimos que llamar a la grúa.

examples.en_text: We had to walk home in the midst of a terrible storm.
examples.target_text: Tuvimos que caminar a casa en medio de una tormenta terrible.

explanation_en: This construction uses the verb 'quedar' in a pronominal, indirect object structure ('no le queda otra [opción] que + infinitive') to express that someone has absolutely no other choice. It is highly common in both spoken and written Spanish across all registers. A common pitfall is forgetting the indirect object pronoun (e.g., 'le', 'me', 'nos') or trying to use 'tener' instead of 'quedar'.

examples.en_text: Since he missed the last bus, he had no choice but to walk back home.
examples.target_text: Como perdió el último autobús, no le quedó otra que volver a casa caminando.

examples.en_text: My computer broke before the exam, so I had no choice but to buy a new one.
examples.target_text: Mi ordenador se rompió antes del examen, así que no me quedó otra que comprar uno nuevo.

examples.en_text: It started raining very hard and they had no choice but to cancel the picnic in the park.
examples.target_text: Empezó a llover muy fuerte y no les quedó otra que cancelar el picnic en el parque.

examples.en_text: Our flight to Madrid was canceled and we had no choice but to spend the night at the airport.
examples.target_text: Cancelaron nuestro vuelo a Madrid y no nos quedó otra que pasar la noche en el aeropuerto.

examples.en_text: I know you didn't want to talk to him, but in the end you had no choice but to apologize to him.
examples.target_text: Sé que no querías hablar con él, pero al final no te quedó otra que pedirle disculpas.

examples.en_text: The director had no choice but to accept the employees' conditions to avoid the strike.
examples.target_text: A la directora no le quedó otra que aceptar las condiciones de los empleados para evitar la huelga.

explanation_en: In colloquial Spanish, 'empalmar' means to connect one event or shift directly to the next without sleeping in between, often used when partying all night and going straight to work or school. It is a very natural, native-sounding verb that is highly common among young people and workers. Be careful with context, as 'empalmar' has other meanings (like joining cables or, vulgarly, getting an erection).

examples.en_text: I went out partying all night and had to go straight through to the morning shift at work without sleeping.
examples.target_text: Salí de fiesta toda la noche y tuve que empalmar directamente con el turno de mañana en el trabajo.

examples.en_text: The students celebrated the end of exams and went straight through to the end-of-year trip without sleeping.
examples.target_text: Los estudiantes celebraron el fin de exámenes y empalmaron directamente con el viaje de fin de curso.

examples.en_text: If you go out tonight, you're going to have to go straight through to your eight o'clock morning class without sleeping.
examples.target_text: Si sales esta noche, vas a tener que empalmar directamente con tu clase de las ocho de la mañana.

examples.en_text: Our flight was so delayed that we had to go straight through to the next day's excursion without sleeping.
examples.target_text: Nuestro vuelo se retrasó tanto que tuvimos que empalmar directamente con la excursión del día siguiente.

examples.en_text: When I was young I could go straight through without sleeping with no problem, but now I need to sleep at least eight hours.
examples.target_text: Cuando era joven podía empalmar directamente sin problemas, pero ahora necesito dormir al menos ocho horas.

examples.en_text: Since he had to deliver the project today, he stayed up all night and went straight through to the morning meeting without sleeping.
examples.target_text: Como tenía que entregar el proyecto hoy, se quedó despierto toda la noche y empalmó directamente con la reunión de la mañana.

explanation_en: The pronominal verb 'volcarse' followed by the preposition 'con' means to devote oneself entirely to helping or supporting someone, or to show immense warmth and solidarity. It is a beautiful, highly empathetic expression frequently used in news reports about community support, charity, or hospitality. A common mistake is using 'por' instead of 'con', though 'volcarse en' is also used when referring to an activity rather than a person.

examples.en_text: The neighbors have gone all out to support the family who lost their home in the fire.
examples.target_text: Los vecinos se han volcado con la familia que perdió su casa en el incendio.

examples.en_text: Everyone in the office has gone all out to support Laura since she got sick.
examples.target_text: Todos en la oficina se han volcado con Laura desde que se puso enferma.

examples.en_text: The citizens have fully rallied behind the food drive campaign for the neighborhood.
examples.target_text: Los ciudadanos se han volcado con la campaña de recogida de alimentos para el barrio.

examples.en_text: We have gone all out to support the new project because we believe it has a great future.
examples.target_text: Nos hemos volcado con el nuevo proyecto porque creemos que tiene mucho futuro.

examples.en_text: The whole town has gone all out to help the tourists who were stranded by the snow.
examples.target_text: El pueblo entero se ha volcado con los turistas que se quedaron atrapados por la nieve.

examples.en_text: The parents have gone all out to support the teachers in organizing the end-of-year party.
examples.target_text: Los padres se han volcado con los profesores para organizar la fiesta de fin de curso.

explanation_en: This is a formal, journalistic collocation used to report casualties caused by disasters, accidents, or wars. The pronominal verb 'cobrarse' literally means 'to collect' or 'to charge', metaphorically treating lives as a toll paid to the disaster. It is an essential vocabulary item for reading Spanish news or discussing current events at a B2/C1 level.

examples.en_text: Last week's earthquake claimed many lives in the south of the country.
examples.target_text: El terremoto de la semana pasada se cobró muchas vidas en el sur del país.

examples.en_text: Traffic accidents claim too many lives during the summer holidays.
examples.target_text: Los accidentes de tráfico se cobran demasiadas vidas durante las vacaciones de verano.

examples.en_text: This serious disease claims thousands of lives every year worldwide.
examples.target_text: Esta grave enfermedad se cobra miles de vidas cada año en todo el mundo.

examples.en_text: The strong tropical storm claimed several lives as it passed through the island.
examples.target_text: La fuerte tormenta tropical se cobró varias vidas a su paso por la isla.

examples.en_text: The conflict on the border has already claimed hundreds of innocent lives.
examples.target_text: El conflicto en la frontera ya se ha cobrado cientos de vidas inocentes.

examples.en_text: The terrible building fire claimed three lives before being controlled.
examples.target_text: El terrible incendio del edificio se cobró tres vidas antes de ser controlado.

explanation_en: This phrase means to be excluded, left out, or to remain outside of a group, organization, or agreement. It is widely used in business, politics, and sports (e.g., being left out of a tournament or squad). It is more active and common than simply saying 'no estar en' or 'ser excluido'.

examples.en_text: The local team was left out of the tournament after losing the last match.
examples.target_text: El equipo local quedó fuera del torneo tras perder el último partido.

examples.en_text: She was left out of the selection process because she did not meet all the requirements.
examples.target_text: Ella quedó fuera del proceso de selección porque no cumplía con todos los requisitos.

examples.en_text: My friends organized a trip for the weekend, but I was left out of the plan.
examples.target_text: Mis amigos organizaron un viaje para el fin de semana, pero yo me quedé fuera del plan.

examples.en_text: Many important details are left out of this new bilateral agreement.
examples.target_text: Muchos detalles importantes quedan fuera de este nuevo acuerdo bilateral.

examples.en_text: If we don't submit the proposal today, the project will be left out of this year's budget.
examples.target_text: Si no entregamos la propuesta hoy, el proyecto quedará fuera del presupuesto de este año.

examples.en_text: Several students were left out of the admission list due to a lack of space.
examples.target_text: Varios estudiantes se quedaron fuera de la lista de admitidos por falta de cupo.

idiom: a lo largo y ancho de
explanation_en: This is a very common idiomatic expression meaning 'throughout the entire length and breadth of' a place. It is used to emphasize that something is happening everywhere within a specific geographic area. It is highly idiomatic and sounds much more natural and sophisticated than simply saying 'por todo el país' or 'en todas partes'.

examples.en_text: We have traveled far and wide throughout Spain this summer.
examples.target_text: Hemos viajado a lo largo y ancho de España este verano.

examples.en_text: The news spread far and wide throughout the country in a few hours.
examples.target_text: La noticia se difundió a lo largo y ancho del país en pocas horas.

examples.en_text: I searched far and wide throughout the house for my keys, but I didn't find them.
examples.target_text: Busqué mis llaves a lo largo y ancho de la casa, pero no las encontré.

examples.en_text: This tradition is celebrated far and wide throughout the region.
examples.target_text: Esta tradición se celebra a lo largo y ancho de la región.

examples.en_text: The company has offices far and wide throughout the continent.
examples.target_text: La empresa tiene oficinas a lo largo y ancho del continente.

examples.en_text: These trees can be found far and wide throughout the forest.
examples.target_text: Se pueden encontrar estos árboles a lo largo y ancho del bosque.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'to blow up' or 'to explode into the air', this idiom is frequently used metaphorically to describe plans, agreements, negotiations, or peace treaties that suddenly collapse or fail catastrophically. It is a vivid, dramatic expression common in political journalism and everyday discussions about failed projects. It is always used with the verb 'saltar'.

examples.en_text: The old warehouse blew up due to a dangerous gas leak.
examples.target_text: El viejo almacén saltó por los aires debido a una peligrosa fuga de gas.

examples.en_text: All our vacation plans went up in smoke when they canceled the flight.
examples.target_text: Todos nuestros planes de vacaciones saltaron por los aires cuando cancelaron el vuelo.

examples.en_text: If we don't reach an agreement soon, the negotiation will go up in smoke.
examples.target_text: Si no llegamos a un acuerdo pronto, la negociación saltará por los aires.

examples.en_text: The police cordoned off the area to prevent the suspicious car from blowing up.
examples.target_text: La policía acordonó la zona para evitar que el coche sospechoso saltara por los aires.

examples.en_text: Their long-term relationship fell apart after that terrible argument.
examples.target_text: Su relación de muchos años saltó por los aires tras aquella terrible discusión.

examples.en_text: The company's secret project went up in smoke when the documents were leaked.
examples.target_text: El proyecto secreto de la empresa saltó por los aires cuando se filtraron los documentos.

explanation_en: This extremely common idiomatic collocation is used to point out something noteworthy or surprising. Instead of using 'es interesante' or 'sorprende,' native speakers naturally use 'llamar la atención.' It can be used with a direct object (e.g., 'me llama la atención') or in relative clauses like 'lo que llama la atención.'

examples.en_text: It catches my attention that the store is always empty at this hour.
examples.target_text: Me llama la atención que la tienda siempre esté vacía a esta hora.

examples.en_text: Her way of dressing always draws everyone's attention.
examples.target_text: Su forma de vestir siempre llama la atención de todo el mundo.

examples.en_text: What struck me most about the article was the last paragraph.
examples.target_text: Lo que más me llamó la atención del artículo fue el último párrafo.

examples.en_text: The poster at the entrance draws attention because of its bright colors.
examples.target_text: El cartel de la entrada llama la atención por sus colores brillantes.

examples.en_text: Doesn't it strike you as strange that he hasn't called all day?
examples.target_text: ¿No te llama la atención que no haya llamado en todo el día?

examples.en_text: This candidate catches our attention because of his extensive experience abroad.
examples.target_text: Este candidato llama la atención por su gran experiencia en el extranjero.

explanation_en: This conjunction is used to express simultaneous progression (as one thing happens, another changes in proportion). It is a key B2/C1 connector that sounds much more sophisticated than 'cuando' or 'mientras.' Note that if it refers to a future or hypothetical action, it must be followed by the subjunctive.

examples.en_text: As you practice a language, you feel more confident speaking.
examples.target_text: A medida que practicas un idioma, te sientes más seguro al hablar.

examples.en_text: As the sun was setting, the temperature began to drop.
examples.target_text: A medida que el sol se ocultaba, la temperatura empezó a bajar.

examples.en_text: As we receive more information, we will keep you informed.
examples.target_text: A medida que recibamos más información, les mantendremos informados.

examples.en_text: As children grow up, they need more space and freedom.
examples.target_text: A medida que los niños crecen, necesitan más espacio y libertad.

examples.en_text: As the train approached the city, the landscape was changing.
examples.target_text: A medida que el tren se acercaba a la ciudad, el paisaje iba cambiando.

examples.en_text: As you read the book, you are going to understand the story better.
examples.target_text: A medida que leas el libro, vas a entender mejor la historia.

explanation_en: The verb 'descartar' means to discard or rule out. Using 'no descarto que' is a very common, elegant way to express possibility in professional, journalistic, and everyday contexts. Crucially, it always triggers the subjunctive mood in the following clause (e.g., 'que haya').

examples.en_text: I don't rule out that we might change offices next year.
examples.target_text: No descarto que cambiemos de oficina el próximo año.

examples.en_text: I don't rule out that it might rain this weekend, so I will bring an umbrella.
examples.target_text: No descarto que llueva este fin de semana, así que llevaré un paraguas.

examples.en_text: I don't rule out that my son will study abroad in the future.
examples.target_text: No descarto que mi hijo estudie en el extranjero en el futuro.

examples.en_text: We don't rule out that apartment prices might drop soon.
examples.target_text: No descartamos que el precio de los pisos baje pronto.

examples.en_text: I don't rule out that she might arrive a bit late to the dinner.
examples.target_text: No descarto que ella llegue un poco tarde a la cena.

examples.en_text: I don't rule out that this headache is due to stress.
examples.target_text: No descarto que este dolor de cabeza sea por el estrés.
